newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cacique gives holidays at coffee plant.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cacique gives holidays at coffee plant.

text.p: Brazil's Companhia Cacique de Cafe Soluvel has given collective holidays at its production plant in Londrina, Parana, because of current high raw material prices in the domestic market, an official said.
Workers at the 1,500 tonne a month soluble coffee plant started 20 days of holidays on May 19, said Elcio Martiniano, raw materials planning and purchasing manager.
"This was due to the price of coffee which does not make it viable for us to operate," Martiniano said.

Brazilian soluble coffee producers have been complaining for some time that high domestic prices mean they risk losing competitiveness given soluble producers in other countries can buy cheaper beans in the international market.
Sector representatives have been examining the issue, with one possible solution special auctions of government stocks just for the soluble industry.
Previously the government has held separate sales of lower quality coffees just for soluble producers at its regular monthly auctions.
But after the last such auction in April, Cacique said it had decided to import 20,000 bags of roasted coffee from India at $67 a 60-kg bag cif to be re-exported as soluble coffee.
The company then gave up the idea "at the request of Brazilian coffee producers and considering the trade balance," Martiniano said.
However if at the end of the collective holidays, no other solution is on the horizon, Cacique may once again consider importing coffee on a drawback basis, he added.
Cacique exports around 1,500 tonnes a month and despite the factory shut-down all export commitments will be met as usual, Martiniano said.
